title: PR #6490 moved structure-board rendering into a new generic render_object_structure admin endpoint and dropped the user_can_change_page check the old details() path applied, so any staff user can read the plugin structure of pages they may not view.

findings.explanation: The diff does not introduce any SQL query construction or user-controlled input reaching SQL queries. Changes involve URL building, middleware logic, model methods, and toolbar utilities. No SQL operations are modified.

New URL patterns registered for object edit/structure/preview endpoints (lines 210-212) that call render_object_edit, render_object_structure, and render_object_preview functions. The patterns accept user-controlled content_type_id and object_id parameters. Without visibility into the implementation of these render_* functions, it's unclear if proper authorization checks are performed. These endpoints appear to bypass standard Django admin permission checks by being registered directly in urlpatterns. CWE-862: missing authorization on protected operations.
findings.suggested_fix: Verify that render_object_edit, render_object_structure, and render_object_preview functions properly check user permissions and ownership before allowing access to arbitrary objects identified by content_type_id and object_id. Ensure these views check object-level permissions and that users can only access objects they own or have explicit permission to view.

findings.explanation: The is_edit_mode() method determines if edit mode is active by checking if the URL name is 'cms_placeholder_render_object_edit'. This is used in line 74 to enable the toolbar. The logic appears to assume that being on this endpoint automatically activates edit mode, but there's no visible authorization check to verify the user has permission to edit that object. This could allow unauthorized users to trigger edit mode.

evidence.content:
if enable_toolbar in request.GET or self.is_edit_mode(request):
            request.session['cms_toolbar_disabled'] = False

findings.suggested_fix: Add authorization checks in is_edit_mode() to verify that the user has permission to edit the object referenced in the current request before returning True. Consider checking object-level permissions before allowing edit mode activation.
